walkthroughs.body_html: On 26 December 2004, a Mw 9.1-9.3 megathrust earthquake ruptured a 1,200 km section of the Sunda Trench, lifting the seafloor by metres. The displacement generated a tsunami that radiated across the Indian Ocean at jet speeds in open water.

Indonesia (Aceh), Sri Lanka, India, Thailand, the Maldives and even East Africa were struck. Approximately 230,000 people died and 1.7 million were displaced. The lack of an Indian Ocean warning system meant that warnings issued by Pacific centres reached few decision-makers.

The Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System became operational from 2006, alongside community evacuation drills and signage. Sendai Framework principles emphasise hazard, vulnerability and exposure. Mangrove restoration, tsunami-resistant building design and education form an integrated response.
